title: Climate Change and Weather Hazards
seo_title: Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science: Climate Change and Weather Hazards Worksheets
standard_code: Earth and Environmental Science Unit 4: Natural and human-induced climate change
standard_text: Evidence for climate change (temperature records, ice cores, sea level); causes and feedbacks; climate models and projections; weather and climate hazards in Australia (bushfires, cyclones, floods, droughts, heatwaves); mitigation and adaptation. (Senior Secondary Earth and Environmental Science, Unit 4: The changing Earth – the cause and impact of Earth hazards)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science worksheets on climate change and hazards: evidence, ice cores, feedbacks, sea-level rise, bushfires, cyclones, floods, heatwaves, mitigation and adaptation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: More greenhouse gases → enhanced greenhouse effect → warming.
key_sub: Mitigation reduces emissions; adaptation copes with the effects.
body_html:
How to think about it

Thermometer records, ice cores, ocean heat, shrinking ice and rising sea level all show warming. The main cause of recent warming is the increase in greenhouse gases from fossil fuels and land clearing; feedbacks such as ice–albedo and water vapour amplify it.

In Australia a warmer climate brings more extreme heat and dangerous fire weather, heavier downpours, longer droughts in some regions and coral bleaching. Responses are mitigation (cutting emissions, renewable energy) and adaptation (planning, building standards, heat plans).

Example

Sea level rose 20 cm from 1900 to 2020. Mean rate?

200 mm ÷ 120 years

Answer: about 1.7 mm per year

Example

CO₂ was 280 ppm before 1800 and is 420 ppm now. % increase?

(420 − 280) ÷ 280 × 100

Answer: 50%

Common mistakes

  • Confusing weather (days) with climate (decades).
  • Saying melting sea ice is the main cause of sea-level rise.
  • Thinking the ozone hole causes global warming.

faq.q: How do scientists know CO₂ was lower in the past?
faq.a: Air bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice cores record CO₂ levels over 800 000 years; levels never went above about 300 ppm before industrialisation.

faq.q: Is a hot summer proof of climate change?
faq.a: No single event proves it, but the long-term trend in temperatures and the increase in extreme heat are clear evidence.

items.q: Which hazard usually causes the most damage when a cyclone crosses the coast?
c: storm surge and flooding, as well as destructive winds
items.e: Cyclone Tracy destroyed much of Darwin in 1974.

items.q: Why is drought a major hazard for Australian farming?
c: rainfall is very variable, and long dry periods reduce crops, pasture and water supply
items.e: The Millennium Drought lasted from about 1997 to 2009.

items.q: How does climate change threaten the Great Barrier Reef?
c: warmer water causes mass coral bleaching, and acidification weakens skeletons
items.e: Mass bleaching happened in 2016, 2017, 2020, 2022 and 2024.
